newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-MATCHES IN THE ENGLISH PREMIER LEAGUE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MATCHES IN THE ENGLISH PREMIER LEAGUE.

text.p: Matches scheduled for this weekend in the English premier league (kick-off times 1500 GMT Saturday unless stated, league positions in parentheses):
Aston Villa (6) v West Ham (17)

Villa were not helped in their quest for a European place when they were beaten 1-0 by Leicester in their last outing. They have doubts over Ireland international defender Steve Staunton (ankle) and England under-21 international Riccardo Scimeca (tonsilitis).

West Ham welcome back Welsh striker John Hartson from a two match man. Striker Michael Hughes begins a three match ban, while midfielder Danny Williamson is out with an ankle injury after a brief substitute appearance in midweek.
Blackburn Rovers (12) v Wimbledon (7)
Wimbledon travel to Ewood Park after their League Cup semi-final aggreagate defeat by Leicester. Coach Joe Kinnear will have a fully fit squad except for long term casualty Ben Thatcher.

Blackburn drew 1-1 with Nottingham Forest on Tuesday and have not lost in their last five games. Caretaker coach Tony Parkes is again likely to be without striker Chris Sutton. Greek winger George Donis could be back after missing two matches through injury as could injury prone Ian Pearce.
Everton (13) v Derby County (14)

Joe Royle's Everton are looking for their first win in five matches. They are without suspended Welsh midfielder Gary Speed while defender Claus Thomsen is doubtful. Ireland defender Terry Phelan (thigh) and midfielder Joe Parkinson (bruised buttock) should be fit.

Derby lost 2-0 to Middlesbrough in the quarter-final of the F.A. Cup last Saturday. Striker Dean Sturridge is suspended. Defender Jacob Laursen (knee) and midfielder Robin Van der Laan (foot) are hoping to be fit.
Leicester City (10) v Middlesbrough (20)

A rehearsal of the League Cup final. Middlesbrough are without suspended midfielder Robbie Mustoe and hamstring victim defender Derek Whyte. Midfield pair Emerson and Phil Stamp are doubtful with ankle injuries.
Manchester United (1) v Sheffield Wednesday (5)

Coach Alex Ferguson will miss suspended midfielder Roy Keane but welcomes back defender Gary Pallister (groin), Welsh international Ryan Giggs (hamstring), Paul Scholes and Nicky Butt. Ronny Johnsen (back) is their only injury absentee.
Wednesday will be without suspended Welsh midfielder Mark Pembridge. Defender Jon Newsome and midfielder Graham Hyde are likely be out for the rest of the season with ankle injuries.
Newcastle United (4) v Coventry City (16)

Forward Les Ferdinand aggravated a hamstring injury after coming on as a substitute in Newcastle's thrilling 4-3 defeat at Anfield last Monday. Striker partner Alan Shearer is still recovering from a groin injury, while defender Warren Barton (groin) and midfielder Robert Lee (flu) will both return.

Coventry have not won in their last six and will be without defender Paul Williams and striker Noel Whelan, who both serve one match bans. Defender David Burrows is in contention for a first team place after three months out with a pelvic injury.
Nottingham Forest (18) v Liverpool (2)

Dutch stiker Pierre Van Hooijdonk makes his home debut after signing from Celtic. Forest's other new signing Ian Moore may play alongside him. Forest hoped to have former England winger Chris Waddle on board but his transfer from Bradford has hit trouble. Midfielders Chris Bart-Williams (knee) and Chris Allen (hamstring) are out.
Liverpool's only doubt is midfielder Michael Thomas (calf) as they continue to press Manchester United at the top of the table.
Southampton (19) v Arsenal (3)

Southampton have gone four games undefeated. Defender Ulrich Van Gobbel and midfielder Matthew Oakley are suspended, while defender Jason Dodd (knee), midfielder Richard Dryden (calf) and recent 500,000 pound ($800,000) signing Micky Evans (ankle) are doubtful.

Coach Arsene Wenger will be without key players for this game. Striker Ian Wright and defenders Lee Dixon and Steve Bould are all banned, while England midfielder Paul Merson (hernia) will be out for six weeks, joining England goalkeeper David Seaman on the injury list. Recent French signing Nicolas Anelka could make his debut.
Tottenham Hotspur (11) v Leeds United (9)
Tottenham are without suspended midfielders David Howells and Allan Nielsen.
Leeds have kept seven premier league clean sheets in their last eight outings. They have doubts over midfielders Lee Sharpe (back) and Rod Wallace, but defender Lucas Radebe returns from suspension.
Chelsea (8) v Sunderland (15) (Sunday 1600 GMT)

Chelsea have taken only two points in their last four league games. French defender Franck Lebeouf is doubtful with a thigh injury, while Nick Colgan, who made his senior debut in midweek, is expected to continue in goal in place of groin victim Frode Grodas.
Sunderland are hoping to sign Danish striker Kim Hieselberg from Aarhus after agreeing a 125,000 pound ($200,000) fee.
